messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] High tail latency detected — europe-central1 (zone-c) edge POPs showing >500ms p99 for generation requests. Automated paging triggered.
lee_sre: got it — paging now. I’m pulling traces and checking ingress/egress telemetry.
maria_prod: seeing a spike in queue depth on the edge pool agents for europe-central1-zone-c; upstream backend instances appear healthy but latency to the cache layer jumped ~6x.
eng_platform: adding context: we rolled a cache GC tweak to edge fleet yesterday at 03:10UTC; telemetry shows increased mem churn on a subset of hosts in zone-c. Could be correlated.
lee_sre: good lead. Can someone confirm if we have partial circuit-breakers kicking? check: `kubectl get pods -n inference --selector=role=edge-pop -o wide` and look for image versions.
maria_prod: running quick query on prod logs now. small subset (~12%) of edge pods in zone-c are reporting repeated KV cache miss flaps and retry floods — looks like server-side cache eviction thrash.
eng_platform: escalating mitigation plan: 1) mark problematic edge node pool as drain-only for new long-running requests 2) bump fallback routing to use europe-west1 edge POPs for affected customer CID ranges 3) deploy a temporary config to increase local cache TTL for seq<=128.
lee_sre: do we have an immediate routing knob? I can push a policy to route non-hard-real-time customers to eu-west while keeping the critical tenants on pinned capacity.
maria_prod: confirmed — policy route exists: `route-policy set --region europe-central1 --fallback eu-west1 --threshold p99>250ms` I can stage it. Recommend we only divert bursty traffic first.
emily_oncall: preparing customer-facing status blurb. Draft below — please sanity check and I’ll cut a statuspage + email: 

```
Customers may experience increased latency for generation requests originating from europe-central1 (zone-c). We are actively mitigating by diverting bursty traffic to neighbouring edge POPs and increasing cache TTLs. No data loss is expected. Next update in 30 minutes.
```

lee_sre: LGTM. Add a line for affected tenants: "Tenants with pinned eu-central placements may see degraded performance; dedicated capacity customers on reserved pools unaffected."
emily_oncall: added. Preparing statuspage update now.
statuspage-bot: [ACTION] Create incident: EU-Central1 edge POP performance degradation — incident ID INC-2026-0321-87. Public status: partial degradation.
emily_oncall: publishing public update and internal note to sales/support with suggested customer template.
lee_sre: mitigation step 1 executed: draining 14 problematic edge pods. Step 2 routing policy staged (will ramp in 2 mins). Observability: p99 dropped from 520ms -> 310ms for rerouted traffic.
maria_prod: cache-ttl bump rolled to 0.25 of edge fleet; need to monitor for any cache-staleness effects (we are only changing TTL for small context requests).
eng_platform: rolling back yesterday's GC tweak on the small subset (hotfix) — patch queued, applying now.
lee_sre: can someone prep an internal comms snippet for ops, sales, and support? quick bullets: impact, mitigation, ETA, customer action. I’ll send handoff to night oncall at 22:00UTC.
emily_oncall: internal snippet (copy/paste): 

"Impact: Partial latency degradation for generation requests in europe-central1 (zone-c). Mitigation: draining affected edge pods, diverting bursty traffic to eu-west1, temporary cache TTL increase, rolling back recent GC change. ETA for stability: 45-90 minutes. Customer action: none required; customers can opt-in to explicit eu-west1 routing if they want shorter tail currently.

Support script: 
- If asked, explain we are diverting non-pinned traffic and working to restore all edge POPs.
- For pinned/dedicated customers, escalate to platform-eng and cc eng_platform.
"

lee_sre: perfect. sending to #support and #sales now.
statuspage-bot: [UPDATE] Public incident page updated: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-0321-87 — message published.
emily_oncall: sending customer email template to support for review: 

Subject: Performance degradation affecting europe-central1 (zone-c) — temporary mitigation in place

Hi —
We’re reaching out to let you know some customers in europe-central1 (zone-c) may see higher than normal tail latency for generation requests. Our engineers are actively mitigating by diverting bursty traffic to nearby edge POPs and increasing local cache TTLs. No data loss is expected. If you are on a pinned/dedicated deployment, you may be unaffected; please reply if you see issues and we’ll escalate immediately.

We will follow up with a progress update in ~30–60 minutes.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Ops

lee_sre: routing ramp looks stable. p95/p99 trending down but still above normal. handing off to night oncall @jonathan_noc — I’ll send detailed logs + playbook link.
jonathan_noc: taking handoff. pls include the list of drained pod IDs and the routing policy revision number. I’ll keep monitoring and notify if we need to expand fallback to other regions.
lee_sre: sent handoff bundle to your DMs. added runbook link: https://confluence.internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/edge-pop-latency
maria_prod: monitoring: after the fixes p99 for region is ~275ms; traffic diversion accounts for 60% of that improvement. continuing to watch KV miss rates.
emily_oncall: posted internal incident summary and next steps to #incidents (private thread) and queued a customer follow-up update for +45 minutes.
lee_sre: closing active paging for this shift — leaving incident open and assigning to jonathan_noc for overnight monitoring. Thanks everyone for fast responses. :thumbsup:
jonathan_noc: acknowledged — I’ll update incident with any regressions or full resolution notice.
